A security update for the bundled SQLite, and a small timing fix.

## Changes

- **SQLite 3.54.1 fixes advisory RUSTSEC-2026-0459 ([#60](https://github.com/DigitalPals/Fusebox/issues/60)).**
  - Fusebox bundled SQLite 3.50.2, which can return uninitialised memory when a database is opened with a crafted `-wal` file. It now bundles SQLite 3.54.1, through rusqlite 0.43.
  - Since SQLite 3.51, one of the usage database's statements was prepared again every time it ran, which made storing usage records 4.7 times slower. Fusebox now keeps each statement's query plan, so the upgrade is a little faster than before instead: on our test machine, storing 100,000 records took 3.4 s (was 3.9 s) and the dashboard's usage summary 29.5 ms (was 34 ms). A test checks the statement is not prepared again.
- **A request's total time is read once.** The usage record and the request log could differ by a millisecond, because each read the clock itself. They now show the same number.

## Upgrading

- **Building from source needs Rust 1.89 or newer** (was 1.88), because rusqlite 0.43 asks for it. The release builds use Rust 1.100, as before.
- **Database.** No change; the usage database stays on schema 5, and an older Fusebox can still open it.
- **No new settings** and no API changes.

Validation: the full Rust, dashboard and Python test suites passed, and formatting, Clippy and the security audit passed; the Release workflow tests the tag on Linux, macOS and Windows.

[Full comparison with v0.17.2](https://github.com/DigitalPals/Fusebox/compare/v0.17.2...v0.17.3).
